should_fail.message: I'll delete slide 1, the cover, expand the pain points into three slides — slides 1, 2 and 3, one per pain point — and change the callout on the techniques slide, now slide 4, to say when to combine few-shot examples with chain-of-thought.

slides.purpose: Introduce the core techniques: give the audience a mental model of prompt design patterns
slides.content_brief: Bullet slide covering the four key patterns — system-prompt framing, few-shot examples, chain-of-thought reasoning, and structured output formatting — with a callout on when to combine few-shot examples with chain-of-thought: a task that needs both a fixed answer format and several reasoning steps
slides.assumes: Audience understands the problem from the previous slide
slides.hands_off: Four composable patterns cover the vast majority of prompt optimisation needs

slides.purpose: Define the problem, pain point 1: inconsistent outputs
slides.content_brief: Bullet slide showing how the same ad-hoc prompt gives different answers from one run to the next, with a callout on what that costs in review time and user trust
slides.assumes: Audience has experienced frustrating or inconsistent LLM outputs first-hand
slides.hands_off: Ad-hoc prompts make a model's outputs unpredictable

slides.purpose: Define the problem, pain point 2: wasted tokens and cost
slides.content_brief: Bullet slide showing how unfocused prompts and retries burn tokens, with a callout on how that cost compounds across every request
slides.assumes: Audience has seen that ad-hoc outputs are inconsistent
slides.hands_off: Ad-hoc prompts waste money on every call
